checks.claim: C1: positive homogeneous covariance distribution as a Radon measure; measure versus density scaling; no atom at the origin; finite even angular measure sigma with factor (2-alpha); locally finite and tempered weighted endpoints; function-class preservation
checks.reason: A nonnegative distribution is a positive Radon measure. Changing variables, the density law gamma(lambda x)=lambda^{-alpha}gamma(x) gives gamma(lambda A)=lambda^{2-alpha}gamma(A) in d=2, which is correct. Applying this to A={0} gives gamma({0})=lambda^{2-alpha}gamma({0}). With 2-alpha>0 and local finiteness, the atom is 0. The sector mass up to radius R is R^{2-alpha}sigma(E)/(2-alpha), which matches the integral of r^{1-alpha}dr from 0 to R times sigma(E). So the (2-alpha) normalization is exact. Evenness of gamma makes sigma even, and sigma(S^1)=(2-alpha)gamma(B_1) is finite. The weight |x|^{alpha-1} gives dr sigma, and |x|^{alpha-beta} gives r^{1-beta}dr sigma. Both are locally finite because 1-beta>-1 when beta<2. Their ball masses grow like R and R^{2-beta}, so both are tempered and integrate |psi| for Schwartz psi. If gamma is in L^1_loc, the weighted objects are L^1_loc functions because their finite ball masses are computed from the same polar form. Function class is preserved.

checks.claim: C2: full-sphere line-mixture factor 1/2; absolute Schwartz Fubini and positive quadratic form; Gamma_low positive definite in d=2; physical angular sigma is distinct from the spectral angular measure
checks.reason: Evenness of sigma gives int f dGamma_low = int sigma(domega) int_0^infty f(r omega)dr = (1/2) int sigma(domega) int_R f(r omega)dr, so the factor 1/2 is correct. For psi=phi*tildephi with tildephi(x)=conj(phi(-x)), the coordinates y=s omega+v give int_R psi(r omega)dr = int_{omega-perp}|int_R phi(s omega+v)ds|^2 dv >= 0. Schwartz decay makes every step absolutely convergent. Integrating against the finite nonnegative sigma gives Gamma_low(psi)>=0, which is tempered positive definiteness. I independently computed the spectral measure of Gamma_low under the source convention gamma(x)=int e^{i xi.x}mu(dxi): it is (4 pi)^{-1} int sigma(domega) times Lebesgue measure on the line omega-perp, so V=S/(2 pi). This shows the physical and spectral angular masses really differ, as the memo warns.

checks.claim: C3: direct line integral of G_h, tangency and a.e. conventions, bound sigma(S^1)/4, preservation under Gaussian covariance and Green averaging; 4ZM=Z sigma is inherited bookkeeping only
checks.reason: G_h^{(2)} matches Chen author (2.5) with d=2. For |b|<h, int_{-A}^{A}(A^2-s^2)^{-1/2}ds=pi, so the line integral is 1/2. Tangency (|b|=h) lies on a set of line-measure zero, and the open-disk representative gives the strict indicator in (LW). Tonelli extends (L) from Schwartz functions to nonnegative Borel functions, which gives (G_h*Gamma_low)(z)=(1/4)int 1_{|z.omega_perp|<h}sigma(domega)<=S/4. The smoothed identity follows from evenness of G_h and p, and from p_eps*p_eta=p_{eps+eta}. A mass-one Gaussian average preserves the uniform bound. As an independent cross-check, the imported lemma bound pi V/2 with V=S/(2 pi) also equals S/4, so the two routes agree exactly. The arithmetic 4 Z_{b0}(S/4)=Z_{b0}S is right, and 1/(k! k^k)<=1/(k!)^2 holds. The memo labels the K_sp=2M and Z_{b0} formulas as inherited bookkeeping, not a theorem. Their sources are not in the packet (see minor findings).

checks.claim: C4: Gamma_st positive definite via the original positive spectral measure times a Gaussian, with absolute mixture/Fubini, no undefined product or fractional power of distributions; homogeneity and Dalang beta<2
checks.reason: The formula |x|^{-lambda}=Gamma(lambda/2)^{-1}int_0^infty s^{lambda/2-1}e^{-s|x|^2}ds is correct for lambda=beta-alpha>0 and x!=0. Since gamma({0})=0, nothing is lost at the origin. Multiplying the tempered measure gamma by the Schwartz Gaussian e^{-s|x|^2} is well defined. Its spectral measure is mu convolved with a positive Gaussian density, so the product is positive definite. Tonelli on |psi| gives int|psi||x|^{-lambda}dgamma<infty from Section 2, which justifies Fubini. Integrating nonnegative quadratic forms then gives Gamma_st(psi)>=0. No fractional covariance power is used. Gamma_st has degree -beta, so its spectral measure scales with degree beta. By Chen-Hu p2146, Dalang under homogeneity reduces to beta<2, and beta<2=d meets Theorem 1.2's range 0<beta<2 wedge d.

checks.claim: C5: parameter interval and affine radial-weight cancellation; Holder on the finite, unnormalized Gaussian-weighted gamma measure; finiteness; common smoothing width; no hidden normalization
checks.reason: The interval alpha0<theta<2-alpha is nonempty exactly when alpha0+alpha<2. On it, theta<1 because alpha>1, and b0=alpha0/theta lies in (0,1). The condition beta>alpha is equivalent to alpha theta>theta, i.e. alpha>1. The condition beta<2 is equivalent to theta<2-alpha. The identity theta(alpha-1)+(1-theta)(alpha-beta)=0 expands to zero. nu_{z,eps} is a finite positive measure because gamma is tempered, and Holder with exponents 1/theta and 1/(1-theta) needs no normalization. The absence of an atom at 0 makes the radial factorization valid nu-a.e. Both endpoint integrals are finite by the polynomial mass growth. The memo explicitly does not certify the all-pairing transfer, the limits, or coefficient summation. It uses the 2eps edge convention of Chen-Hu p2152 and Chen author p13 consistently.

checks.claim: C6: exact admissibility of the original d=3 covariance, radially lowered F mass and tempered properties, short fixed-Gaussian box lower bound with constants, boundedness of a Gaussian-smoothed PD covariance, contradiction; no full moment no-go
checks.reason: gamma=|x1|^{-9/10}|x2|^{-3/5} is in L^1_loc, even, nonnegative, and homogeneous of degree -3/2. A product Gaussian mixture shows it is positive definite, because each Gaussian constant in x3 is a PD function on R^3. 0<3/2<3 and 3/2+1/4<2 place it in Hypothesis H:homog and the Chen author (1.5) range. F=|x|^{1/2}gamma has degree -1, ball mass growing like R^2, and int(1+|x|)^{-N}F<infty for N>2. On Q_L: |y|>=L; |y1|^{-0.9}|y2|^{-0.6}>=2^{-3/2}; |z_L-y|^2<=9; and the volume is 1. Hence (p_1*F)(z_L)>=2^{-3/2}(2 pi)^{-3/2}e^{-9/2}L^{1/2}. If F were PD, p_1*F would be the continuous Fourier integral of the finite positive measure e^{-|xi|^2/2}mu_F, so it would be bounded by its value at 0, which is finite. That is a contradiction. The claim boundary (not a moment no-go) is stated.

checks.claim: C7: longer shifted-sphere cross-check: projection normalization, beta integral and divergence, Gaussian approximate identity with polynomial-mass tail, null exceptional sets, Fatou, correct use of the degree-one lemma
checks.reason: Each hemisphere has Jacobian (1-u^2-v^2)^{-1/2}, and 2/(4 pi) gives exactly G_1^{(2)}. The substitution h=1-u gives 1-u^2=2h-h^2. Then v=sqrt(2h-h^2)w produces the factor (2h-h^2)^{-a2/2} times int_{-1}^{1}|w|^{-a2}(1-w^2)^{-1/2}dw=B((1-a2)/2,1/2)=B(1/5,1/2). The lower bound 2^{-3/10}h^{-6/5} diverges at 0. Also |y+z|>=2 on the shifted sphere, so F>=sqrt(2)gamma there. The tail inequality p_eps(v)<=(2 pi eps)^{-3/2}e^{-delta^2/(4eps)}e^{-|v|^2/4} holds for eps<=1, |v|>=delta. Local continuity of F off the planes plus the order 'eps to 0, then delta to 0' gives pointwise convergence when x1x2!=0. The exceptional set is one point plus a great circle, both null. Fatou needs no monotonicity. The degree-one lemma (internal-input.tex) needs nonnegative, even, PD, degree 1 with 0<1<3, h=1, eta=0 allowed. All of these hold under the hypothesis that F is PD, so its uniform bound pi V_F/2 contradicts liminf=infinity.

checks.claim: C9: source variational M is finite: Chen-Hu (1.11) p2147 and p2175 citation and identification; Chen 2023 Theorem 1.1 on p2 explicitly finite under Dalang; penalty comparison and parameter use; source theorem imported, not re-proved
checks.reason: Chen-Hu (1.11) defines M with penalty int|grad g|^2 over F_d with unit L^2 norm. P2175 invokes [11] Theorem 1.1 and displays sup{(...)^{1/2}-(1/2)int|grad g|^2}=2^{alpha/(4-alpha)}M, exactly as transcribed. Chen 2023 p2 Theorem 1.1, under Dalang (1.3), states 'the variations appearing on the right hand sides of (1.4) and (1.5) are finite'. Its F_d coincides with the unit-norm W^{1,2} class. The penalty comparison is valid: for every g, A(g)-int|grad g|^2 <= A(g)-(1/2)int|grad g|^2, so M is at most the finite supremum. The application to the planar static endpoint is explicitly made conditional on independent validation of its PD. Dalang for degree beta<2 comes from Chen-Hu p2146. The FIXME header is transcribed accurately and is mathematically immaterial.
